frames.narration: Today the API returns a user as { name: 'Ada Lovelace' }. The old mobile app and others read 'name'.
Product wants firstName and lastName instead. If the API simply replaces 'name' with the two new fields, the old app breaks the moment you deploy.
Safer: add the new fields but keep 'name' (marked deprecated). Nothing a client relies on has changed, so no new version is needed.
Some changes cannot be additive, for example a different structure for addresses. Then you publish /v2 and keep /v1 running unchanged.
Both versions are served from one internal model. The API translates between that model and each version's shape, so a bug fix is made once.
v1 responses now carry Deprecation and Sunset headers. You watch v1 traffic fall as clients migrate.
When v1 traffic is gone or the promised date has passed, you retire it. Clients that ignored the notices break, which is why you measure first.
